prompt:
You are controlling a network client (Telnet). Your instruction: Say hello to the server, then answer each question it asks with a short answer. When it says BYE, disconnect.

# Response Format
Return ONE JSON object {"actions": [ ... ]} holding every action to perform now, in order. Return {"actions": []} to do nothing now (or `wait_for_more` when a reply is incomplete and more is coming). JSON only — no prose, no code fences; an optional <reasoning>…</reasoning> block may precede it.
`set_memory` / `append_memory` keep notes that are shown to you as "Memory:" on every later call; what happened earlier in this session is shown above the event when the client keeps history.

# Available actions
send_command

Send a text command to the Telnet server (a newline is appended)

Parameters:
- command: string (required) - The command text to send (newline will be appended)

Example:
```json
{
  "type": "send_command",
  "command": "ls -la"
}
```

send_text

Send raw text to the Telnet server, exactly as given and with no newline added. Use it where the server is waiting mid-line.

Parameters:
- text: string (required) - The text to send

Example:
```json
{
  "type": "send_text",
  "text": "yes"
}
```

wait_for_more

Send nothing and wait for the server's next write. Use it when what arrived is only part of a prompt or a banner.

Example:
```json
{
  "type": "wait_for_more"
}
```

disconnect

Disconnect from the Telnet server

Example:
```json
{
  "type": "disconnect"
}
```

set_memory

Replace this server's (or client's) memory with new content; the old memory is discarded. Memory is shown to the model with every event, is shared by all of the instance's connections and outlives each one, unlike the history of a single connection, which ends with it. Keep here anything needed later by every connection: data you stored, counters, settings.

Parameters:
- value: string (required) - New memory value as a string. Replaces all existing memory.

Example:
```json
{
  "type": "set_memory",
  "value": "users_created: alice,bob\nnext_order_id: 1043"
}
```

append_memory

Add lines to this server's (or client's) memory; existing memory is kept. A line written `key: value` replaces an earlier line with the same key instead of adding a second one. Memory is shown to the model with every event, is shared by all of the instance's connections and outlives each one.

Parameters:
- value: string (required) - Text to append as a string, one fact per line. A `key: value` line replaces the earlier line with that key; any other line is added after the existing memory.

Example:
```json
{
  "type": "append_memory",
  "value": "connection_count: 5\nfiles_uploaded: 3"
}
```

notify_operator

Show a note to the person operating NetGet, on their own screen. It is NOT sent over the network: the peer, client or server on the other end never sees it. To say anything to them, use this protocol's own send or response action.

Parameters:
- message: string (required) - The note for the operator (never transmitted)

Example:
```json
{
  "type": "notify_operator",
  "message": "Server #1 is listening on port 8080"
}
```
